dishes.name: Papet vaudois
dishes.desc: Leeks stewed with potatoes until soft, served with a smoked Vaud sausage (saucisson vaudois or saucisse aux choux). The canton's signature winter dish, found in country restaurants and at autumn butcher events.

dishes.name: Taillé aux greubons
dishes.desc: Flaky savoury pastry studded with pork cracklings, a Vaud bakery classic since the late 19th century. Eaten at aperitif time or with a bowl of soup.

dishes.name: Malakoff
dishes.desc: A deep-fried cheese fritter with a soft, molten centre, born in the La Côte villages around Vinzel and Luins. Served hot with salad or as a snack in local cafés.

dishes.name: Vacherin Mont-d'Or
dishes.desc: Soft, spruce-banded winter cheese made in the Vallée de Joux and the Jura of Vaud, eaten baked in its box with potatoes. Sold only from autumn to spring.

dishes.name: Perch fillets
dishes.desc: Small lake perch fillets, pan-fried in butter and served with fries or potatoes and lemon. A staple of the Lake Geneva shore restaurants from Lausanne to Vevey and Morges.

dishes.name: Salée au sucre
dishes.desc: A round of yeast dough topped with cream and sugar, a Vaud bakery and village tradition, listed in the canton's living-heritage inventory with the raisinée tarts. Best eaten warm.
